newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian directors expect further rate cut.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian directors expect further rate cut.

text.p: More than 50 percent of Australian company directors expect local interest rates will decrease and that inflation will remain steady, a survey released on Monday showed.
The September 1996 national quarterly survey of Australian company directors also indicated a preference toward investment in new equipment and information technology.

Covering the spectrum of opinion from large to small enterprisies across all industries, the survey reported that interest rates have fallen to third place as a factor affecting profits behind demand for product/services and labour costs.
Only 8.0 percent of directors reported interest rates were likely to rise.

Announcing the results of the "The Boardroom Report", John Harkness, executive chairman of consultants KMPG said a major trend since June was a movement from 'above' budget to 'on' budget expectations by directors.
Forty-eight percent of company directors anticipate profits 'on' budget, compared with only 38 percent last quarter.
Of these 56 percent of directors from the mining/agriculture sector and 53 percent of directors from the construction/utilities expect profits 'on' budget.

The overall outlook of directors from the construction/utilities and the wholesale/retail sectors has improved significantly, reflecting better prospects for these industries occassioned partly by the July 30 interest rate cut.
Directors also expressed increased confidence about the Australian economy with 70 percent indicating they expect the economy will improve over the next 12 months.

The survey showed 34 percent of directors plan to invest up to A$0.5 million, from 29 percent in the previous quarter, while 52 percent reported an intention to invest in new eqipment in the next 12 months, including 83 percent in manufacturing.
Thirty-nine percent of directors intending to invest in the next 12 months would be investing in information technology, including 49 percent of directors in the business/financial services sector.
